header.scope: Readonly host19; allvisible mainprocess stat/schedstat and own-descendantQEMU allthreads/affinity/wchan every0.5s. Namespace may omit external contenders. NoPMU/stacks or scheduler/config writes.

baseline.scope: ThreadCPU/schedstat for QEMU; /proc/PID/stat CPU includes process threadgroup for visible main process records. Do not sum the process record and its thread records. schedstat/wchan remain per selected task, not threadgroup. Endpoint spans are explicit, not identical to guest sampled endpoints.

post_rejit.scope: ThreadCPU/schedstat for QEMU; /proc/PID/stat CPU includes process threadgroup for visible main process records. Do not sum the process record and its thread records. schedstat/wchan remain per selected task, not threadgroup. Endpoint spans are explicit, not identical to guest sampled endpoints.

proc_stat_semantics: Linux fs/proc/array.c do_task_stat(whole=1) uses thread_group_cputime_adjusted for /proc/PID/stat, so direct process CPU includes helper threads but excludes children. /proc/PID/task/TID/stat and schedstat/wchan describe the selected task. Prior main-process-only caveat applies to per-thread state/schedstat visibility, not omission of helper-thread CPU from process-group stat counters.
host_limits: Current PID namespace may hide other host contenders; absent visible competitor is not absence of contention.
Guest boot-clock alignment uses a single date+uptime pair; host realtime-minus-monotonic bounds and snapshot enumeration durations are retained.
No PMU or historical host wait data are inferred; current host/guest data cannot prove cause of old3x180s anomaly.
limits: Main-process /proc entries only, not every thread; tool helper threads can be missed.
One0.5s snapshot enumerates tasks sequentially, so its timestamp is not an atomic per-task instant.
Wait/stack counts are sampled observations, not exact blocked durations.
CPU deltas cover only first-to-last observations of a PID/starttime identity, never child CPU counters; short-lived tasks and tails can be missed.
The observer adds syscalls/9p output and potential BPF work; its own CPU does not bound its kernel/tracing impact.
One10s pair cannot establish the cause of historical3x180s results or throughput acceptance.
